report:
Findings:  Small joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Intact lateral meniscus. Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with both radial and horizontal components.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band, pes anserine tendons and popliteus tendon. Multi loculated ganglion cyst encasing the popliteus tendon, measuring approximately 4.8 cm in CC dimension.  Intact extensor mechanism. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  Focal high-grade chondropathy in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle with underlying bone stress change, and a similar smaller focus noted were anteriorly. Relatively well-maintained hyaline articular cartilage in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Low-grade chondral thinning and minor bone stress changes noted along the median patellar rate and medial retropatellar facet.  
Conclusion:  Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with both radial and horizontal components. Degenerative changes in the medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartments as described. Ancillary findings described above.

MRI RIGHT KNEE

INDICATION: Pivot twist, exquisite pain with weightbearing/pivot

Routine MRI of the right knee shows extensive degenerative signal in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is a nondisplaced degenerative tear at the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Medial meniscus is peripherally extruded 2 mm along the medial jointline.

No lateral meniscal tear. ACL and PCL are intact. Tiny hairline intrasubstance tear in the distal quadriceps tendon. Patellar tendon intact. There is slight edema about the MCL in keeping with a mild sprain. Lateral collateral ligaments are intact.

Small joint effusion. Mild prepatellar bursitis. No Baker's cyst. No cartilage defects. No bone bruises.

IMPRESSION:

Nondisplaced degenerative tear at the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Large amount of intrasubstance degenerative signal in the body of the medial meniscus with no surfacing tear.

Mild MCL sprain.

Tiny hairline tear in the distal quadriceps tendon.

No bone bruises.

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. A small free edge radial tear of the body of lateral meniscus is noted. Normal medial meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild generalized thinning of the tibiofemoral compartment articular cartilage. Focal fraying of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage is noted with mild underlying bony change. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Small free edge radial tear of the lateral meniscus. No medial meniscal tear. Mild tibiofemoral and patellar chondral the as described.

MRI of right Knee with

> Obliteration of anterior horn of lateral meniscus with linear signal intensity inside and displaced fragment, reflecting lateral meniscus tear.
> Abnormal signal intensity is noted in posterior aspect of lateral femoral condyle, which shows low signal intensity on T1WI and high signal intensity on T2WI, in favor of bone marrowe edena with suspicious of small osteonecrosis causing small hypointensity line in subchondral region (srs: [ID].
> Interstitial increased signal of ACL on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury or degeneration.
> The contour of PCL, MCL, and LCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Some intermediate signal intensity intra-articular foci in right knee joint (srs: [ID]; the largest one about 2.2*1.1 cm in size.
> Wearing of articular cartilage ( more severe at lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau) and spur formation of right knee, reflecting osteoarthritis.
    Wearing of articular cartilage of patella, in favor of grade 2-3 chondromalacia.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over anterior aspect of right knee.

Impression: 
1. Tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee, more severe at lateral compartment.
3. Synovitis of right knee with  suprapatellar bursitis and synovial chondromatosis ( in favor of loose bodies); patellar plicae.
4. Bone marrow edema in lateral femoral condyle with R/O small osteonecrosis in subchondral region.(srs: [ID].
5. Grade 1 injury or degeneraiton of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus of right knee as current injury, initial encounter; right knee pain since injury [DATE] during soccer, contact with another player and heard a pop 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with small fragment displaced towards the meniscotibial recess.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the lateral facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Partial-thickness tearing near the jointline.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Oblique tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with small displaced fragment towards the meniscotibial recess.
2.	Grade 2 sprain of the medial collateral ligament, near the joint line. 
3.	Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Lesión meniscal.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Rotura degenerativa de la raíz meniscal posterior y parte del cuerno posterior del menisco medial
con leve extrusión meniscal.. Esto se asocia discreto edema las partes blandas regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial lateral sin alteraciones. Cartílago troclear dentro de
límites normales. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y prácticamente total de distribución difusa
de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular. Laminar cantidad de liquido intermuscular en la región posteromedial de la
rodilla.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura degenerativa de la raíz meniscal posterior y parte del cuerno posterior del menisco medial
con leve extrusión meniscal. Edema de las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular

Trouvailles :

Il y a un épanchement intra-articulaire modéré avec synovite. Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité.

Il y a légers changements dégénératifs avec amincissement du cartilage et fibrillation superficielle plus proéminent au niveau du compartiment interne. Il n’y a pas de région de perte de cartilage complet.

Il y a changements dégénératifs intra-substance avec macération et extrusion du ménisque interne. Il y a une déchirure horizontale surajoutée à la corne postérieure s’étendant à la surface articulaire inférieure du ménisque. Il n’y a pas de fragment déplacé. Le ménisque externe démontre une déchirure horizontale focalisée à la corne antérieure et au niveau du corps. Il n’y a pas de fragment déplacé.

Autrement, le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et tendon du poplité, le biceps fémoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion :

1. Légers changements dégénératifs un peu plus proéminents au niveau du compartiment interne.

2. Changements dégénératifs intra-substance avec macération et extrusion du ménisque interne avec déchirure horizontale. Il y a aussi une déchirure horizontale du ménisque externe. Aucun fragment déplacé.

3. Épanchement intra-articulaire avec synovite sans kyste poplité.

There is a minor knee effusion. The posterior medial meniscus is attenuated in size. No definite tear is identified. A tiny free edge radial tear is noted in the posterior body of the lateral meniscus.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is well preserved. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Attenuated posterior medial meniscus but no definite tear. Small free edge radial tear of the lateral meniscus.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Three-month history of nontraumatic left posterior knee pain. Ultrasound suggests medial meniscal tear. Assess for internal derangement   .

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

There is splitting of the fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament unassociated with thickening or deficiency. The finding is favored to represent a described but rare anatomic variant. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is intact and unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint appears to be reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The medial meniscus is intact. Involving the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus there is some contour flattening of the inferior margin of the meniscus peripherally suggesting possible deficiency of a portion of the meniscotibial ligamentous attachment. There is no evidence of a significant medial meniscal tear. Articular cartilage of the medial compartment is reasonably well-maintained. There is fraying seen to the posterior surface of the weightbearing surface of medial femoral condyle consistent with moderate focal chondrosis.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. Fibers appear mildly attenuated compatible with a remote partial-thickness sprain. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Projecting in the intercondylar notch surrounding the anterior cruciate ligament, situated anterior to the posterior cruciate ligament there is a multiloculated ganglion cyst measuring about 1.9 cm in length and 1.5 x 1.3 cm in short axis. The finding is consistent with an anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

The medial collateral ligament is intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no evidence of a significant Baker's cyst. A small 8 x 4 mm ganglion cyst is seen projecting posterior to the proximal tendon fibers of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Moderate chondrosis to the medial joint compartment associated with contour flattening of the inferior surface of the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus. This finding is equivocal but could indicate presence of partial deficiency of the meniscotibial attachment in this region. No discrete medial meniscal tear is identified.

Mild attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with remote partial thickness injury. Associated anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

Suspected congenital duplication of the medial patellar retinaculum.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Artrosis leve. Quiste de Baker.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento de baja señal del
componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial. El resto de los componentes sin
alteraciones.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios que de rotura.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial medial y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial de la faceta lateral.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano y de la inserción distal del tendón
cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas , profundo a los tendones de la pata de ganso.
Impresión:
Leve engrosamiento secuelar del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Condropatía rotuliana superficial de la faceta lateral.
Signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal y cuadricipital distal.
Probable laminar bursitis profunda a los tendones de la pata de ganso
